title: Repair F938/F929 event units for fuel, shields and hull repair
finding: main.rs passes combat::frame_tics into spend_thrust_energy/recharge. F152 divides elapsed tics by 0xc22e and dispatches event 6 through F151 to F1007; F1007 passes the whole-second count to F938. At 1x the port charges about 49,700 times the source rate. This explains early internal-fuel warnings and disabled acceleration.
acceptance: Trace one reserve from fresh type-0 boot through idle, 0x24 climb, full thrust, firing and 1x/10x/10000x. Match source event counts, energy, warning time, limit restoration, shields and repair; preserve wrapping arithmetic.
progress: 2026-10-26: F938/F929 executed-source comparison now passes 192 cases (reserve, shields, hull, wrapping arithmetic, fuel and waste). Whole-second live events retained; exact F152 scheduler alignment remains open.

title: Make reserve refuelling and cargo fuel bookkeeping match F929/F903
certainty: Confirmed bookkeeping mismatch; reserve initialisation is correct
finding: The internal reserve is object +0x11e and correctly starts at 0x20000000. It is distinct from cargo fuel, although thrust and lasers use the same source reserve. Flight::burn_fuel removes military fuel without adding radioactive waste; the jump helper does add it. Do not invent separate rechargeable laser and engine pools.
acceptance: Compare hydrogen and military auto-refill with/without Auto Refueller, full/empty reserve, zero-cost call, full hold, waste and cargo-used words, including after save/load. Verify jump cargo is debited exactly once.
progress: 2026-10-26: 192 executed F938/F929 cases match reserve, hydrogen, military fuel and waste. Existing jump tests retain F903 cargo burn. Full warning/limit restoration and scheduler traces remain.

title: Use one authoritative fitted-drive and failure state
finding: Damage/service code changes combat.drive while drive_state prefers nonzero loadout.drive. Thus a damaged/destroyed drive can still supply the old hyperdrive class, and reserve fuel selection can disagree with the jump report.
acceptance: Destroy, degrade, service, remove and fit each drive; compare engine limits, gauge, fuel type, range, jump refusal and reload with the original object +0xd0.
progress: 2026-10-26: Jump class now reads object drive state without resurrecting a removed/integral drive from statistics. Damage, degradation, servicing, save migration and escape inheritance agree with that state. Damage/save/outfitting checks pass; full source scenario trace remains.

title: Translate the complete F1013 takeoff handler and same-frame mode order
finding: F1013 runs F1037, changes 0x24 to 0x26 before F1041 when its tests pass, and explicitly calls F602. The port updates Takeoff after its physics tick and Player::step_in normally chooses capped F601 when engines are on. The fixed up-thrust is therefore not sufficient evidence of source launch behaviour.
acceptance: Replay type-0 and type-1 launches: no keys, held Return/Shift or selected port control mapping, speed change at threshold, engine-off and failure cases. Compare every frame mode, set/actual speed, thrust, cap, velocity and position.
progress: 2026-10-26: F1013 now transitions on previous altitude/current set speed before F1041 and always uses uncapped F602, including transition frame. Runtime defers F1031 until the next handler. Boundary and real Hope launch regressions pass; full source frame replay remains.

title: Replace launch altitude substitution and collision grace with source frame/contact rules
finding: The runtime substitutes climb from a stored seat for DATA_008867, suppresses landing scans for 120 presented frames, and inhibits the source frame selector in its small pad world. Launch safety consequently depends on frame rate and adapters rather than source contacts.
acceptance: Prove pad release, planet retained, rotating/linear transforms, re-touch, high acceleration and return-to-pad on real ports; compare F1033 altitude and flags. Remove grace only when those traces pass.
progress: 2026-10-26: Confirmed omitted F1677 rotation in navigator surface-port positions/orientations. Corrected rotating-to-root conversion removes immediate 680 m false contact altitude. Live handoff no longer uses measured seat climb. Collision grace/frame-selector suppression remain open.

title: Verify original set-speed controls, input gates and speed persistence end to end
certainty: Confirmed differences; reported dead acceleration also depends on PAR-01
finding: Modern W/S is default while source Return/Shift is selectable. HeldControls adds release gates. Landed F1039 correctly excludes throttle, but launch must enable F1037 immediately. OriginalFlight reconstruction derives nonnegative set speed from actual forward velocity, losing negative or independently selected speed; cancel has both halt-to-zero and actual-speed paths.
acceptance: Record physical key -> mapped key -> active/mode -> F1121 set speed -> thrust -> actual velocity. Test fresh key after intro, held intro key, launch, autopilot cancel, engines off, reverse speed, menus and reload. Source controls are default; optional mappings belong only in Port Options.
progress: 2026-10-26: Signed selected speed persists independently of actual velocity through save/model rebuild. New settings default to Classic; saved preferences preserved. Remaining input/cancel/source-replay checks are open. 2026-11-02: DATA_008866 is written only by the new-game set-up (0) and read by F1018 and F750, so the autopilot cancel always zeroes the set speed; the port's cancel does that, and OriginalFlight::from_flight's forward-speed fallback applies only to states without a saved set speed (older saves). Key-to-thrust replay checks remain.

title: Match the original Hope starting state and cockpit view to the supplied image
certainty: Confirmed visual mismatch; exact spatial cause not yet established
finding: Correct system/planet names do not prove matching bay, seat, rotating frame, eye offset, city model, orientation or lighting. Current source F994 copies station rows, sets +0x57=1 and calls F650; the port uses a fresh bay allocation and a linear pad world. The screenshot shows the expected broad city/runway view, unlike the close building face. Do not guess a new coordinate or camera angle.
acceptance: Dump actual default type 0, not the Ross 154 type-1 probe: clock/RNG, station slot/model, bay table, ship rows/frame, seat, eye, visible objects and projection. Compare identical 320x200 front frames at 12:00:01 against executed original and the user image.
progress: 2026-10-26: Original executable default-start frame reproduced and matches user image. Found and fixed missing F997 half-turn and missing F994 temporary bay-1 sentinel (wrong bay 1 vs source bay 0). Camera now faces source city layout. Atmosphere/ground colours and exact projection remain visually different.

title: Restore the complete third-person player explosion before GAME OVER
certainty: Confirmed lifecycle/camera mismatches; exact blue-mesh primitive needs capture
finding: F1104/F1105 select the explosion object as camera reference and set external distance 0xf9000000. The port switches view but retains the old ship as reference, keeps ordinary own-ship rendering and its existing external distance. Effects use a fixed lifetime and forced global 4=0x4000 rather than source object evolution. This is not equivalent to F942 followed by the external explosion hold.
acceptance: Capture non-capsule player death at source event-relative times: removed old ship, correct explosion reference/distance, animated fragments, debris, palette/depth, sounds and 0x3cae6 wait, then tombstone. Identify the blue mesh by model/primitive trace; test crash, laser and missile death separately.
progress: 2026-10-26: F1105 camera now follows explosion axes/motion, uses source 0xf9000000 external distance and suppresses removed player hull. Effect age, mass-global and lifecycle parity remain open; no claim that blue mesh is fixed.

title: Replace orbital docking corridor tests and harmless pushes with source contacts
finding: Port::contact accepts a 15%-of-face corridor (minimum 60 m), 250 m/s entry limit and teleports/rezeros bad approaches without source damage. Navigator::contact calls this in normal player flight. Original collision/clearance/pad tests must decide docking and crashes.
acceptance: For every station model compare cleared/uncleared entry, bay, hull/slot edge, angular mismatch, moving station and entry speed; same damage, bounce, law/traffic and dock transition. No guessed corridor or silent position reset.
progress: 2026-11-02: the corridor test, 250 m/s limit and teleporting 'pushed clear' are gone from normal flight. Inside an orbital station's hull radius the ship flies in the station's rotating frame for each tick and F569/F570/F575 scan the station's collision stream; F1021/F1024's rule reads the result (region 0x20 with a soft touch 0x40 and no crash: dock when cleared, F1022's warning and the 0x24 climb when not, the pad-1 bay check), and a hull strike is F575's crash/bounce with F953 damage. tests/station_dock.rs: entering the slot on the axis gives 0x22 then 0x62, 120 m off the axis at 200 m/s gives 0x80 outside the region. Still open: F595's station orbital velocity (the tick does not subtract it), per-station-model and moving-station comparisons against the executed original. Spin: the scan uses the station's rows at the current clock (F866's spin applied to its base rows, as drawn), and a ship in the station's scan turns with the station frame to frame (F572's co-rotation: at rest in the rotating frame unless it thrusts), so the slot tested is the slot on screen and the station holds still around the ship. The autopilot's final-leg roll alignment uses the same spun rows. The station's orbital motion is carried by the navigator's frame following.

title: Use original indoor departure placement and moving lift/door state
finding: Port::launch_point places the ship front + 2*radius + 2 km away. Launch-grace suppresses hull collision until clear, and the ship is held by port sequence adapters. Timed lift stages alone do not verify release position/velocity/orientation.
acceptance: Compare source door stages, bay, object placement and velocity on every release frame for rotating and nonrotating stations; remove spatial grace/teleport substitutions.
progress: 2026-11-02 source reading: F1088 (mode 0x22 -> 0x36 for an indoor station, +0x14c & 0x20 clear) zeroes the player's +0x3e..+0x52 and sets z = 0x10000 (65.5 m along the station's own axis, in its frame, +0x57 = 1), runs F1042/F1093, negates rows 0 and 2 and sets +0x1b8 = 0xfffff4a3 for models 0x45/0x4f (else 0xb5d), sets the station's +0xc9 = 0xff and door word +0x9e = 0xffff. Mode 0x36's movement handler F1030 is empty: the ship stays there while F1089 waits for the door word to reach 0, then sets mode 0x26 (F1031: the player flies out under F1037/F1041/F601 with F1033's scan; 0x26 holds while the scan reports region flag 0x20, then mode 0). An open-air port (0x20 set) takes mode 0x38 with the ship copied to the port's position and rows (F1520), then F1090 -> 0x24. The port's launch_point teleport and spatial grace replace all of this; porting it needs the ship to fly inside the station's rotating frame (KNOWN_ISSUES 'Station velocity is not ported'). 2026-11-02: the launch seat is now F1088's (0, 0, 0x10000) in the station's rotating frame (65.5 m along its forward row) instead of the station's centre, and the exit runs F569's scan in the station frame like any other flight there; the spatial collision grace is gone. While the scan reports the region the ship is in mode 0x26 (F1031: no docking test), and leaving the region (about 2 km out on the test station) ends it. Still approximate: the door wait happens in the lift stages rather than with the ship parked at the seat, the ship's facing is the port's docking axis rather than the rows F1088 keeps (with F1088's row negation for models 0x45/0x4f), and F595's orbital velocity is not applied.

title: Complete source autopilot world and target adapters
finding: Live player ordinary F597/F587/F589 arithmetic is verified, but F610/F802 avoidance, accelerated near-offset physical-frame matching, rotating-parent F589, ship targets and object-event cadence are missing. Prototype helpers remain developer-only and their arrival tests are not player parity evidence.
acceptance: Replay full planet approach, obstruction, moving ship pursuit, all station docking models and 1x through 10000x without direct turns or long-leg teleports; same event/state/contact sequence.

title: Unify source event clocks, time acceleration and physical integration
finding: The frame loop, fixed prototype accumulator, whole-second events, AI updates and 0.1 s physics clamp use different scheduling paths. TICS_PER_SECOND is 49700 while F152 uses 0xc22e=49710. High acceleration can advance clocks/events without equivalent collision/frame work.
acceptance: Same scripted input and RNG consumption at 20/50/60/144 fps, pauses, focus loss and acceleration boundaries; distinguish source timer domains and reproduce event ordering, not merely elapsed calendar time.
progress: 2026-11-02: timer domains checked: the clock runs at 0x3e2/20 = 49,700 tics/s (TICS_PER_SECOND) and F152's whole-second events every 0xc22e = 49,710 tics (THINK_TICS); both are kept as distinct constants. Scheduler/frame-rate replay remains.

title: Complete hyperjump initiation, transit, misjump and source arrival
certainty: Confirmed gameplay substitute; core fuel formula not shown wrong
finding: F903 standalone range/fuel/time arithmetic uses model mass, as does current drive_state: do not replace that with guessed wet mass. Navigator::hyperspace instantly advances time and chooses an offset from the first planet, skipping the source transition and arrival placement.
acceptance: Replay normal/military drives, exact and insufficient cargo, out of range, mode/altitude refusal, cancellation/failure/misjump, clock/cargo/waste and source arrival RNG/position. Compare consumption as a transaction with no debit on refusal.

title: Verify source fuel scooping gates and capacity changes
finding: The playable uses nearest-star surface distance, floating speed conversion, a cooldown and port cargo-capacity accounting. Helper threshold tests do not establish F1033 contact/class, atmosphere, heat, cargo-used and timing behaviour.
acceptance: Sweep contact flags, altitude, speed, fitted/mounting state, fuel species, full hold, pause and acceleration; compare exact increment events and heat/damage with the original.
progress: 2026-11-02: F1033 read against the port: star contact model range, fitted bit, 30 km, speed 0x2328, the 0x2468a-tic interval, the used/capacity test, 0x9906 and the silent sample 0x11 ('nowt') match. The missing hull temperature (DATA_008804+0x1ec) is ported: F1033's star heat (tics>>8 for 0x8c+, >>10 for 0x89+) and F1007's whole-second cooling (<<9/<<7). The star contact is the port's 30 km surface test, not F569's contact flag; no executed trace yet. F1014's speed heating is ported as a helper but not run in flight: F1035 below 20 km reaches only the empty F1017, and F1014 is called from the landed handlers F1011/F1012. F1014's speed heating (JJFFE form: shift 0x16/0x13 by Atmospheric Shielding, cap 0x1000, burn above 0xffff, 0x99e6 on crossing 0x8000) is a tested helper but is not run in flight: F1035 below 20 km reaches only the empty F1017, and F1014 is called only from the landed handlers F1011/F1012.

acceptance: Trace traders, escorts, pirates, police and heavy freighters under the same objects/seed; match per-state target, thrust, turn, velocity and event time at 1x and accelerated time.

This changes threats, speed selection, bays and other outcomes on reload. Native file encoding itself need not change gameplay.

The --capture-save round trip is byte-equal with three ships and a station record. Missiles in flight, effects, the shared RNG words and the integer OriginalFlight/control state are still rebuilt rather than restored.

certainty: Confirmed independent RNG/lazy-generation deviation; individual formulas may match

title: Drive all explosion, debris and hit effects from source object states
finding: Effect::tick integrates floating velocity and removes objects after port-chosen lifetimes. Renderer supplies a fixed explosion input instead of F764/F769 growth/state evolution. This affects the destruction scene, visibility and object recycling/RNG as well as appearance.

certainty: Integration fidelity still unproven; source constants alone are insufficient

title: Remove silent fallback to the synthetic playable from normal starts/loads
finding: Navigation/model creation converts errors to None and original=None permits Flight::step synthetic physics. That alternative must remain developer-only; a missing asset/frame adapter must not silently change player movement, safety or docking rules.
acceptance: Inject missing/invalid essential cache records and unsupported saves; the normal game must report a concrete error or source-equivalent recovery, never enter prototype physics. Dev tools remain explicitly gated.
progress: 2026-10-26: Source navigation initialization and flight errors propagate instead of silently falling back to prototype. Legacy/prototype save and developer entry paths still need complete audit. 2026-11-02: free flight builds the original model whenever a frame reaches the flight step without one; only --dev's O chord selects the prototype physics. Missing models/statistics are a start-up error outside --dev instead of the placeholder station and stand-in limits. Legacy-save import is still not offered (no specimen).

title: Use the same source new-game setup after death and on every resume path
finding: After GAME OVER the new-game branch sets cash/ship and Mode::Docked, original=None, but does not apply the initial pad seat/rows/model setup used by the first boot. This can restart in a different view/state and expose the synthetic fallback.
acceptance: Compare initial Enter boot, post-death Enter boot, alternate start, intro load and escape/resume paths: identical source fields, seat/rows/frame, HUD, model, input release, fuel and services before the first tick.
progress: 2026-10-26: Initial boot and post-Game-Over new commander call one source pad/equipment/ship initializer. Both start types remain parked for 600 frames; F997 and bay sentinel also apply after restart. Full live death/restart/resume replay remains. 2026-11-02: the post-GAME-OVER new game now also resets the commander record (ranks and slots carried over before) and the rest of the first boot's per-game state: engines and status pages, status section/scroll, a pending jump, held time acceleration, the landed pose, the gear warning, the beam hold and the targetter arming. Equipment and combat words already came from the one new_commander initializer.
